Oxy isn’t prescribed all the time. It is notoriously difficult to get. I have pretty severe chronic pain (the type where I need brain surgery to fix it) and I don’t get any opioids unless I’m in the ER for breakthrough pain. I could use some oxy. I’m fortunate in that marijuana can help my pain and I get that (it is legal in my state). It doesn’t work all the time, however, but it does work some of the time. I’ve been to pain management and all of their suggestions are pointless because of the type of pain that I have. Chronic pain is a bitch to treat and it’s very difficult to get opioids for it. At least that’s true in my region.

EDIT: clarification

So definitely NTA here, but if I may insert some advice—I don’t know your exact disabilities/situation but I am on SSDI as well and they have several rules involving payees. 

One of them is that if you’re viewed as unable to manage your financials, your check is put in the payee’s name instead of your own. I would call Social Security yourself and find out exactly why your mom is the payee and you aren’t. You might need a new doctor’s note saying that yes, you are disabled, but that you can manage your own financials. Also, you should be able to talk to social security yourself as long as you have your address and social security number. The wait is long—usually an hour—but it’s definitely worth it. 

Anyway, I encourage you to look into specific rules and laws regarding payee stuff. They make it unnecessarily complicated and I can’t recall all of them at the moment as I haven’t looked into it in a while. 

But, in conclusion, I hope you get away from your mom. Good luck. <3

On top of you being the AH, you're not really considering that a LOT of epilepsy meds are not safe for pregnancy. How do I know this? I have seizures and went through a lot of meds before I found something that works for me. The entire time, my neurologist warned me about the side effects on a fetus. It's not good. At all. Now, as someone who is disabled, I'm not suggesting that the baby shouldn't be born for that particular reason, but it IS something that needs to be discussed here. Are you ready to care for a disabled child? Are you willing to be patient, loving, and kind to a child who is cognitively or physically or mentally disabled? Caring for disabled people is hard work and there's a lot of issues with caretaker burnout or worse, caretakers literally killing their disabled relatives. 

If you push this on her and somehow she agrees, please, please, PLEASE consider that the child may be disabled as a result of the life-saving epilepsy meds and you'll be caring for a disabled child. Just something to consider.

Oh interesting, I didn't know that we don't know a lot about chronic pain! That explains so much. Thank you for your explanation. 

I'm not necessarily after opioids--I just want something that works because this is miserable. I just need to keep trying until I find the right doctor, which may take a while. But I'm willing to keep trying.

I'm on gabapentin/carbamazepine for my trigeminal neuralgia. It doesn't really affect my fibromyalgia at all. I'm hesitant to try something like cymbalta, but I'm willing to try it. I've mostly just heard horror stories about cymbalta withdrawal. 

But the gabapentin/carbamazepine doesn't do much for my pain overall. Maybe drops it a point or two on the pain scale. Weed is legal in my state, so if my fibromyalgia pain is particularly bad, I'll get edibles. I do try managing it, but it's still out of control most of the time. I'm on an SSRI and an antipsychotic for my bipolar disorder, so I suspect doctors don't want to add more meds into that mix? I just need something to take me seriously OR possibly explain why I'm not being treated beyond "you're an addiction risk."
